agent_trace.summary: On brain MRI, acute infarcts are usually identified as focal areas of restricted diffusion and often localize to a specific vascular territory in the cerebral hemispheres. The visual cues here (cerebral hemispheres, cortical ribbon, subcortical white matter, and midline falx) support evaluating for unilateral or bilateral hemispheric lesions, with laterality being a key descriptor. The retrieved SLAKE chunks are only weakly supportive of a left-sided location and should not be treated as definitive for the infarct location.

key_facts: Acute infarcts on MRI commonly appear bright on diffusion-weighted imaging and dark on ADC maps due to restricted diffusion.
Hemispheric infarcts may involve the cortical ribbon, subcortical white matter, or both, depending on vascular territory.
Laterality (left, right, or bilateral) is important for describing infarct distribution in the brain.
The midline falx helps distinguish unilateral from bilateral hemispheric involvement.
Acute ischemic lesions often follow an arterial pattern rather than crossing midline structures.
